newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak maintenance workers reject arbitration.
newsitem.headline: Amtrak maintenance workers reject arbitration.

text.p: The Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employees said Tuesday it has rejected the National Mediation Board's offer to arbitrate the union's dispute with Amtrak.
"On September 4 we will shut this railroad down if we do not have a contract," said Jed Dodd, General Chairman of the Pennsylvania Federation that includes the majority of the union's Amtrak members.
With the rejection of arbitration, a 30-day countdown starts after which either party is free to turn to self-help, the BMWE's statement explained.
The BMWE is the labor union which represents the workers who build, construct and maintain Amtrak's railroad tracks, buildings and bridges and overhead catenary system.

Amtrak, as the National Railroad Passenger Corp is commonly known, owns the Northeast Corridor stretching from Washington to Boston and west to Harrisburg, Pa., from Philadelphia. Those tracks are used by Conrail -- now owned by CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp -- to deliver freight to much of the U.S. Northeast.

Amtrak workers traditionally receive the same wage increases won by maintenance of way workers on the nation's other Class 1 railroads. That contract, settled a year ago, keeps real wages -- or wages adjusted for inflation -- at 1988 levels.
"Maintenance of way workers are fighting just to keep up," said BMWE President Mac Fleming.

BMWE members have worked without a general wage increase for more than two years. Contract talks opened in November 1994. After months without any progress, negotiations entered mediation in December 1995.
